query: What review signals predict low Yelp user satisfaction?

per_column.name: staff_rudeness_or_indifference
per_column.rationale: A specific service-quality complaint signal extracted from review text; it lies outside the label and plausibly predicts low satisfaction without being a restatement of it.

per_column.name: excessive_wait_or_slow_service
per_column.rationale: Slow-service complaint is a distinct experiential feature that carries predictive signal about satisfaction and is not a deterministic function of the label.

per_column.name: staff_inattention_or_neglect
per_column.rationale: Captures a specific negative service dimension; a legitimate predictor of label_pos rather than a component of it.

per_column.name: poor_taste_or_flavor
per_column.rationale: Food-quality complaint is an orthogonal content signal that plausibly predicts dissatisfaction; not leakage since it does not restate the label.

per_column.name: staff_forgot_or_ignored_table
per_column.rationale: A concrete neglect event extracted from text; a valid predictor with real signal about low satisfaction, distinct from the label itself.

judge.rationale: All five added columns are semantically specific negative-experience signals (service, wait, attentiveness, food quality) derived from review_text but not derivable from label_pos itself, so they avoid leakage and restatement. They target the driver dimensions of dissatisfaction the query asks about and provide genuine predictive leverage beyond the raw text. Utility is high but not maximal because the features are heavily skewed toward staff/service themes, leaving other dissatisfaction dimensions (price, cleanliness, ambiance) uncovered, which limits coverage as a set.
